title: llm-gemini 0.37
text: Release: llm-gemini 0.37 Google launched Gemini 4 Hydrogen today - the lowest cost member of the Gemini 4 family. It's actually not too far off the price of its much bigger siblings, Carbon and Argon. I'm finding Gemini 4's pricing really confusing. Here's the pricing scheme: Model Dates Input ($/M) Cached input Output Gemini 4 Carbon Through Nov 30, 2026 $2.00 $0.10 $10.00 From Dec 1, 2026 $4.00 $0.20 $20.00 Gemini 4 Argon Through Nov 30, 2026 $2.00 $0.10 $10.00 From Dec 1, 2026 $4.00 $0.20 $20.00 Gemini 4 Hydrogen $1.50 $0.075 $7.50 Carbon and Argon are the same price , and both are scheduled to double in price on December 1st. If they're the same price, why have two different models? Google says that Argon "delivers Gemini 4 intelligence with faster responses and lower token spend per turn compared to Gemini 4 Carbon" - so it may be priced the same, but it will use less tokens per task. Hydrogen, supposedly the cheap model, is currently only a 25% discount on its more capable peers. The Hydrogen price will make more sense after December 1st, when it will represent a 75% discount. It's still considerably more expensive than Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna - they're both $0.10/$0.50, so Hydrogen is 15x that. I had Hydrogen generate some pelicans . Here's a full comparison grid showing the pelicans for all three members of the Gemini 4 family at their three supported effort levels: Considering how close they are in price, the difference in pelican quality for Hydrogen is quite stark. Here's how Google describe Hydrogen's intended position in their mix of models: In real-world software development, while teams rely on frontier models like Carbon and Argon for deep architectural judgment when designing systems or untangling subtle bugs, they still need a fast, disciplined execution model for writing code, running tests, and verifying changes. Hydrogen is built to stand on its own as a model for everyday work — or to pair with Carbon and Argon as the high-efficiency execution engine in multi-model workflows. Most notably, Hydrogen is the new free tier model, and is the model that will power AI features in Google Search. Tags: gemini , llm , google , pelican-riding-a-bicycle , llm-pricing , ai , llms

title: AI Ambition: ArtCraft Cloned Photoshop and Now Wants to "Rebuild Everything"
author: Richard MacManus
text: The theme of day two of the AI Engineer Code Summit in San Francisco was increasing ambition using AI . And there have been few projects as ambitious as ArtCraft in the AI era. So far the fledgling company has released 17 open source versions of popular software tools , starting with a Photoshop alternative built from scratch in Rust called PhotoCraft . You could feel the excitement in the room this morning when ArtCraft founder and CEO Brandon Thomas presented a kind of manifesto for AI-based open source at AIE Code. When he mentioned that ArtCraft had cloned Adobe’s Acrobat, with a product called PdfCraft, it got a round of applause from the audience. In wrapping up, his rallying cries of “let's take back the entire internet” and “let's rebuild everything” were greeted with whoops and cheers. Thomas began his presentation by reliving the internet’s early history. In his view, the web started out with the right intentions, but things got screwed up once Web 2.0 hit the mainstream. “We had a bunch of chat applications that were completely open,” he said, regarding the 1990s internet. “So, IRC is like Discord, but you can spin up your own servers that you actually own. You can use whatever programs to automate them and interrogate them without rules.” His point wasn’t necessarily that everything was open source, but that web users could freely build things. With Flash, for example — a commercial animation tool eventually acquired by Adobe — “kids were making all kinds of animations.” When Web 2.0 came along, with its superior broadband and smartphones, “it brought everybody into the fold.” Thomas acknowledged that this widened the scope of internet software, but at the cost of that freedom to build with leading apps. “The diffuse, experimental, early web started to disappear,” he said. “The APIs got taken away from us, and then we started seeing distribution being gatekept by the big providers.” It seems Adobe in particular annoyed Thomas. He described getting billed with an unexpected fee when he cancelled a monthly plan. “It's really frustrating that the web — that was once really, really promising and open and free — has turned into this extractive, owned, rent-seeking world.” This inspired him to start ArtCraft, “with the ethos of ‘let's build everything open source.’” A message even anti-AI people have gotten behind, according to Thomas. In addition to PhotoCraft, they’ve copied other apps in the Adobe suite, cloned Figma, and created a Microsoft-like word processor called WordCraft. There are also independent apps such as SolidCraft, a community-led CAD project distributed through ArtCraft’s launcher. Thomas reiterated that these AI-built applications are 100% open — “not only the desktop apps, but the actual infrastructure as well.” PhotoCraft: The development process ArtCraft is starting with rewriting familiar tools. Thomas’s longer-term vision is for users (such as artists who were previously using Photoshop) to tailor the software to their own workflows. As he framed it, they want to “undo what had happened during Web 2.0 , when everything became owned and consolidated and gatekept, and just give people back their applications.” AI is the means to achieve that, he said. But aren’t there already open source alternatives to Photoshop, like GIMP? “GIMP isn't really used by artists,” said Thomas during his presentation. “We actually observed artists vibe coding their own workflows on top of the software that we gave them.” To begin creating PhotoCraft, the team gave an AI model a detailed prompt outlining Photoshop’s tools, data structures and file importers. After that, they “laid out a large, large prompt to say, let's build out the application.” As part of that process, they made everything MCP and CLI compatible . title: WAWTECH 2026 już wkrótce
text: To kolejna edycja warszawskiej konferencji technologicznej organizowanej przez DOU. Na konferencji pojawi się ponad 90 prelegentów i przeszło 3000 uczestników z Polski oraz innych europejskich krajów. Wydarzenie przyciąga przede wszystkim deweloperów, tech leadów, product managerów, data scientists i specjalistów od AI oraz ML. W programie znalazło się sześć ścieżek: - Main, - AI, - Dev, - Startup, - Product, - Future. Organizatorzy zapowiadają wystąpienia dotyczące product mindsetu oraz tworzenia agentów AI. Będzie też mowa o tym, dlaczego jedni inżynierowie przechodzą rekrutację, a inni odpadają. Nie wszystko wydarzy się w salach wykładowych. W planie są strefa warsztatowa, roundtables z prelegentami, Job Speed Dating i osobny Meetup Day. Na żywo zostanie nagrany także odcinek podcastu "Shit I Know Live", a wieczorem odbędzie się afterparty z koncertem zespołu DakhaBrakha. Na scenie będzie można posłuchać takich prelegentów jak: Daniel Stenberg (cURL), José Valim (Elixir), Mariusz Gąsiewski (Google), Vlad Sydorenko (OpenAI), Ivan Lapa (Netflix), Artem Chernodub (Zendesk), Taras Kloba (Microsoft), Hanno Embregts (Oracle ACE Pro), Radek Wojtysiak (Allegro), Dmytro Kovalenko (Dropbox) oraz Dima Maleev (Agoda). Wśród wystawców znajdą się m.in. Bolt, Preply, SQUAD, Waymo, Capital.com, Ciklum, Creatio, iPlan, N-iX, Nord Security, PostgreSQL, Shelf, Solidgate i Svitla Systems. Tuż obok będzie działać strefa gastronomiczna z loungem. title: [AINews] Jensen Huang resigns after 33 years leading NVIDIA
author: swyx .ai
text: Congrats to Gemini 4 Hydrogen on their launch and it seems Anthropic’s IPO is well under way, but today’s headline was only ever going to be about one thing, the most earthshaking leadership change in AI (after Demis/Jeff/et al at Google DeepMind). Yesterday we covered reports that NVIDIA’s board was preparing to replace Jensen Huang following an NYT report of an affair with an accused Chinese spy . Following news of a second affair , today NVIDIA announced his resignation (correlation/causation is debatable here), presumably forced by the board: View post on X ↗ There is also some discussion of the extent that Chinese models can demonstrably be shown to be trained on Blackwell GPUs that they should not have access to… though the scale is debated . After 33 years, Jensen Huang has stepped down as CEO, president and boardmember. Colette Kress, NVIDIA’s CFO since 2013, will keep that job while serving as interim CEO… leading into what will presumably the best attended earnings call in the history of $NVDA next week. AI News for 11/11/2026-11/12/2026. We checked 12 subreddits, 544 Twitters and no further Discords. AINews' website lets you search all past issues. As a reminder, AINews is now a section of Latent Space . You can opt in/out of email frequencies! AI Twitter Recap Gemini 4 Hydrogen: Google's Fast Gemini 4 Tier Ships Broadly Launch : Google DeepMind released Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a speed-first model positioned alongside Carbon and Argon. Google says it completes tasks 2.5x faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash and edges Argon on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, 51 vs 50 at default thinking and 54 at the new xhigh level ( DeepMind , Koray Kavukcuoglu ). Specs and pricing : The model offers four thinking levels (low, medium, high and xhigh) and a 1M context window. It costs $1.50/$7.50 per million input/output tokens, with a 95% discount on cached input ( Phil Schmid , Artificial Analysis ). Official claims : Google reports 57% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 and more than 3x Gemini 3.8 Flash on Terminal-Bench 4.1. It also claims more than 5x fewer fabricated claims, #1 on Vals Tax Agent Bench and leading results on AutomationBench-AA and Agents' Last Exam ( Google ). Availability : Hydrogen is available on all Gemini API tiers, including a free tier in AI Studio. It is the default model in Search AI Mode, and free Gemini app users get it through auto-selection. Paid Pro and Ultra subscribers can use it in Antigravity ( Sundar Pichai , GeminiApp , Search ). Orchestrator multi-model mode : In Antigravity, Carbon plans while Hydrogen writes and tests code. Google says this reaches near-Carbon success on Terminal-Bench 4.0 with 24% less quota and 19% faster completion. It is rolling out to Ultra subscribers ( Google , Mohan ). Artificial Analysis measurements : The independent results show a mixed profile. Intelligence and cost : At xhigh, Hydrogen scores 54, one point behind Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max) and GPT-6.1 Sol (max). Its cost is about 32% of Sonnet's but about 2.5x Sol's. Cost per task is $3.16 at xhigh and $1.87 at high. Output speed is about 200 tok/s ( AA ). Strengths : Hydrogen has an 8% hallucination rate on AA-Omniscience, versus 43% for Sonnet and 52% for Sol. It also shares the #1 score on GDP.pdf visual reasoning. Weaknesses : It scores 54% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 at both high and xhigh, below Sonnet at 64% and Sol at 56%. Third-party leaderboards : Agent Arena : Hydrogen debuts at #5 with +14.8% net improvement across 6.5k sessions. It is the fastest model in the top 10 at 5.3 minutes per task median, with a median cost of $1.6 per task ( Arena ). Code Arena WebDev : It ranks #10 with 1703 points ( Arena ). Vals Index : It is #6 at 68.5%, 2 points behind Carbon at 38% of Carbon's price ( Vals ). Coding agents : CursorBench rises to 54.3% from 39.6% for 3.8 Flash ( Cursor ). Cognition's FrontierCode 2.0 shows 38.2%, just behind Sol ( Cognition ). SWE-sweep shows 13.5%, versus 9.5% for Astra ( KLieret ). Caveats from users :
